stories.headline: Juniper Ridge drops three first sets and wins 6-1 at Liberty Hill
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Ezekiel Amoore walked to the fence at Liberty Hill Monday a set down, 6-1 to junior Jaxton Martin, and coach Ray Okafor stayed on the bench. Amoore won the next two sets 7-5, 6-3.

Defending 5A champion Juniper Ridge won the opener 6-1, and two more of its singles players came back after losing the first set. Okafor picked Amoore for first singles after a week of trying different players there. "He was tight for a set," Okafor said. "After that he wasn't."

Levi Chesnut, the sophomore who went 16-0 as a freshman, lost the first set 6-3 to Ethan Cross at No. 4 singles and won 12 of the last 14 games. Senior Jonah Smith did the same at No. 5, 4-6, 6-0, 6-4. Deon Rennick (6-3, 7-6) and Joshua Butcher (6-3, 6-1) won in straight sets at second and third singles.

Liberty Hill's point came at No. 1 doubles, where seniors Brooks Marco and Kannon Benito beat Gabriel Clark and Avery Hermes 7-6, 2-6, 6-4. "They've played together since middle school," Liberty Hill coach Gary Tomczak said.
Juniper Ridge (1-0) is home Tuesday against Pacersburg and Wednesday against Westfield Friends.

stories.headline: Dukes wins 6-1, 6-1 in his first match at the top for Altamonte
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Altamonte coach Paul Ostrowski moved Roman Dukes, a senior who played doubles nearly all of last season, to first singles over the summer. Dukes beat Cranston Diggins 6-1, 6-1 Monday, and Altamonte swept Senator Gray 7-0 in the crosstown opener.

Grant Labbé, who played first singles a year ago and went 8-23, asked for the change in June, Ostrowski said. "He told me Roman would win more up there than he did." Labbé moved down one place and beat John Jensen 6-2, 6-4.

Dorian Sadiq, Liam Mochizuki and Michael Crawford won the last three singles positions without dropping a set. Two freshmen, Reed Fong and Carter Fiore, won 6-4, 6-2 at No. 1 doubles, and Joe Curran and sophomore Michael Williams came back from a first-set tiebreak at No. 2 to win 6-7, 6-2, 6-4.
Altamonte opens BBL play Saturday at Anse Doree. Senator Gray plays at Bitterroot Wednesday and at Ditch Fork Thursday.

stories.headline: Six of the first 12 go 4-3
body: Calder. It won eight duals a year ago and beat Central West End, a state octofinalist last fall, 5-2 at home. Freshman Kostas Maniatis and sophomore Leroy Ryang beat seniors Isaiah Conway and Lucas Pogba 7-6, 7-5 at No. 1 doubles, then sat on the fence by the court for an hour watching the last singles match. Junior Charles Williams beat Nico Buchner 6-1, 7-6 at first singles.

Marlow County. It won 4-3 at Carolina Island with points from two freshmen: Muhammad King at No. 5 singles (6-3, 7-5) and Abram Conn, who partnered senior Denis Strelkov to a 6-3, 6-3 win at No. 1 doubles. Sophomore Troy Holmes lost his first set 6-1 at third singles and won 6-1, 6-2.
Aspen Hollow. It also won 4-3, at Seamus Town, where freshman Andre Salaun beat Mason Perez 6-4, 7-6 at fifth singles.
The rest of the 4-3s. Copper Gap over Cornerstone Christian, Telfair Country Day at Doyle Pass, Trout Lake at Star Hollow and Fountain Park at Meridian Regional.
Silton Ridge. The Desert Sky champion lost all seven matches at Espoo.
California Canyons. Hudson Chiu lost a first-set tiebreak to Rohan Lancaster and won 6-2, 6-1 in a 5-2 win at Summervale.

stories.headline: DCL play opens Tuesday, the Kajaani and Desert Sky Thursday
body: Marlow County opens DCL play at home Tuesday against Archbishop Quinlan. Calder hosts Obama Wednesday, Trout Lake hosts Cornerstone Christian, Central West End plays at Frontier and California Canyons at Pomar.
Thursday, Copper Gap plays Aspen Hollow in the Desert Sky, Juniper Ridge opens the Kajaani at Cedar Exchange and Liberty Hill is at Tidewater Catholic.
